edits.modify_from: (3) walk the frames after the first container frame in order and keep a running slot assignment. A SHUFFLE is a maximal run of consecutive frames in which two containers are off their slots (well over 10 pixels); it ENDS at the first later frame where all containers are again at slots. At that ending frame, swap the slots of the two containers whose slots were empty during the run. Keep walking: if a later frame again shows two containers off their slots, that is a NEW shuffle, even if it is the same two slots as before, and it swaps them again when it ends. Before computing the answer, write out the list of shuffles in order (e.g. 'shuffle 1: slots P and Q, frames 80-96, ends 112; shuffle 2: slots P and Q, frames 128-144, ends 160'). Two shuffles of the same pair put them back where they started; three leave them swapped. Shuffles of other pairs do not change the named container's slot;
edits.modify_to: (3) go through EVERY container frame after the first one, in order, up to and including the last demonstration frame, and label each frame before doing anything else: either 'all at slots' or 'slots P and Q empty' (a container is off its slot when it is well over 10 pixels away). Do not stop at the first 'all at slots' frame and do not stop before the last frame; the final shuffle can sit in the frames just before the closing frames. Then group consecutive 'empty' frames into runs; each run is one SHUFFLE, and the number of runs is the number of shuffles, however many there are (one, two, three or more) and whether or not the same pair of slots repeats. Write out the list of shuffles in order (e.g. 'shuffle 1: slots P and Q, frames 80-96; shuffle 2: slots P and Q, frames 128-144; shuffle 3: slots Q and R, frames 176-192'). Then keep an explicit slot table (which container is at which slot, starting from the first container frame) and apply the shuffles one by one in time order, each time swapping the two containers whose slots were empty in that run, writing the table after every swap. Only after the last shuffle is applied read off the named container's slot. Parity cross-check, not a substitute: for the named container's pair, an even number of shuffles of that pair returns it to where it was before those shuffles, an odd number leaves it swapped; if the table and the parity disagree, recount the runs. Shuffles of pairs the named container is not in do not change its slot;
